ours: each chord is 6 cm from the centre
note: PROOF, derived a third time from the stem alone (radius 10, chord 16). The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so the half-chord is 8 and the distance d satisfies d^2 = 10^2 - 8^2 = 36, d = 6 (an exact integer square root). BOTH candidates tested against the stem's own datum: d = 6 implies a chord of 2*sqrt(100-36) = 16, exactly what the stem states; d = 12 is IMPOSSIBLE and self-refuting, because 12 > radius 10, so a line at that distance misses the circle entirely and there is no chord at all (r^2 - d^2 = -44). The key's 12 is 6 + 6, i.e. the distance BETWEEN the two chords when they lie on opposite sides of the centre - the answer to a question the stem does not ask ('distance of these chords FROM THE CENTRE'). No misalignment of the key is involved: PS 6.2's entry (2) = 24 cm matches Q2 exactly, so entry (1) is genuinely Q1's, and there is no question before Q1 for it to have shifted from.

book: Prob 6 (1)(vii) 'D or B' - printed verbatim as a two-option hedge, confirmed on the rendered page at 3x
ours: D (7 cm)
note: The key is TOO GENEROUS rather than wrong: it contains the correct option and also admits one the stem excludes. Derived a third time from the stem alone (radius 5; chords 6 cm and 8 cm; 'on opposite sides of the centre'): half-chords 3 and 4 give distances d1 = sqrt(25-9) = 4 and d2 = sqrt(25-16) = 3. On OPPOSITE sides the centre lies between the chords, so the separation is d1 + d2 = 7 cm = option D. On the SAME side it would be |d1 - d2| = 1 cm = option B. The stem states opposite sides, so B is excluded by the stem's own stated configuration and D is the only admissible answer. The remaining options are dead either way: C (8 cm) exceeds the maximum possible separation d1 + d2 = 7 for these two chords, and A (2 cm) matches neither configuration. Our key D is the correct half of the printed hedge; the defect is that the key reproduces the answer to a configuration the question rules out.
